block.title: wide filmstrip: trench eel breach and gyre volley
block.positive: SNES-era 16-bit pixel art sprite filmstrip on a flat deep-navy background, wide horizontal sheet, bold dark navy outlines, saturated limited palette, dithered shading, no scene, no text, no labels, no UI. Two horizontal filmstrips stacked with a clean margin. Upper strip, seven frames of a TRENCH EEL breach facing left: a flat deck-line with a thin violet glow seam, deck seam widening, blunt tooth-ridged snout clearing the lip, first three ring-plates out in an S-curve, half the body reared, full arc with mouth open spitting one violet ring-spark, and the settle-back frame with only the snout and a closing hatch glow remaining — same eel design in every frame, only the body height and mouth state changing. Lower strip, six frames of a GYRE ring-gun volley: the gun-metal ring with four rim muzzles rotating clockwise, muzzle number one flashing amber, two, three, four in consecutive frames with one small orange projectile leaving the fired muzzle each time, and a sixth frame where the ring spins free with all muzzles dark and a thin smoke wisp off the hub. Consistent amber top-light, hard readable silhouettes at game scale.
block.negative: text, labels, numbers, watermark, photorealistic, 3d render, scene background, gradient background, blurry, inconsistent character design, silhouette changing between frames, merged frames, extra enemies, blue-green lighting, pure black background, perspective distortion
block.notes: Color reference: eel glow seam and sparks #b84cff, muzzle flashes #e8a030, projectiles #f06820. The numbered-muzzle clause ("one, two, three, four in consecutive frames") is the load-bearing trick of this entry — without it the rotation and the firing order blur into noise and the strip can't be sliced.
